question: Risk screening in ANC is a one-time assessment at the booking visit that classifies a pregnancy as high-risk or low-risk for the remainder of the pregnancy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct reasoning. Risk status must be reassessed at every ANC contact because new complications (e.g., gestational hypertension, GDM) can arise at any gestational age, even in initially low-risk women.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: That is actually incorrect. Risk screening is a dynamic, ongoing process — a pregnancy that is low-risk at booking may develop complications at any subsequent contact.
